basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Statistics produced under a public mandate with documented methods, quality and release rules.
Each observation keeps its vintage, so revisions never overwrite what was published earlier.
Differs from a generic dataset by its authority, public-purpose claim and disclosure control.
References respondent and source records but never exposes microdata.

may: Retrieve published series with their vintage, unit and method notes.
Explain concepts, classifications and quality indicators to users.
Report a suspected error to the producing agency.
Compare vintages to show revision history.
mustNot: Access or release statistics before the official release time.
Attempt to re-identify respondents from published tables.
Present an estimate without its stated uncertainty or provisional status.
Describe unofficial figures as official statistics.
requiresHuman: Granting access to confidential microdata for research.
Changing a published method or classification.

considerations: Respondents provide data on a promise of confidentiality that must be kept.
Professional independence protects statistics from political pressure.
Groups that are poorly counted become invisible in policy.

items: An official statistic carries a producing authority, a series code, a reference period, a unit, a vintage and a release date.
It is confused with administrative data, commercial survey results and derived estimates by third parties.
Policy errors from misreading provisional or revised figures.
Loss of trust when revisions are not explained.
SDMX 3.0 for statistical data and metadata exchange.
DDI for survey and microdata documentation.
UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics and European Statistics Code of Practice.
